children: Council on Foreign Relations senior fellow Ray Takeyh said renewed Houthi attacks are a significant setback for the U.S. strategy of stabilizing regional oil flows and may point to closer coordination between the group and Iran, according to Bloomberg.

Takeyh also told hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini that economic pressure has failed to force Tehran to change course, while new construction at the deeply buried Pickaxe Mountain complex has raised questions about the future of Iran's nuclear program.

title: GEOPOLITICS | Takeyh Says Houthi Attacks Set Back U.S. Oil-Flow Strategy
